audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart and the full-layer phases gave Levels 2, 3, First item and 2+ items to Kennen, while whys[1], whys[2], whys[5] and whys[6] all state Gnar wins exactly those stages, and phases[6].why says 'your pattern is at full power'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar and the win rate is 52.61% — Gnar-favoured. Every prose field already agreed; only the sides were wrong.
audit.corrected: win[1], win[2], win[5], win[6] and the matching phases[N].side flipped to Gnar with ratings raised. Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 left as Skill — the Rage-RNG and Slicing Maelstrom framing genuinely makes those coinflips.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built on 'track Lightning Rush' and 'all-in when it's down', with no cooldown given for anything.
audit.why: Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6 seconds — far too short to plan an all-in around; it is an escape, not a window. The punishable cooldown in this matchup is Slicing Maelstrom, a flat 120 seconds at every rank, and that is the one the reader should be counting.
audit.corrected: 120s written into whys[4], mid and breakdown.cooldowns; Lightning Rush demoted to what it is, with its 6-10s range stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text warns about 'three Marks for a stun' repeatedly but never says which abilities apply them, so the reader cannot count. Electrical Surge's on-hit application and Lightning Rush's exit attack speed were absent from both layers.
audit.why: Mark of the Storm stuns on the third mark, and Thundering Shuriken, Electrical Surge and Lightning Rush each apply one — the stun only exists when all three are available, which is the actual thing to deny. Electrical Surge applies on-hit and Lightning Rush grants attack speed on exit, so his damage scales with attack speed and armour reads the trade wrong; the page already says build MR but never says why.
audit.corrected: Mark sources named in early; the on-hit / attack-speed scaling added to late.
sources: enemyKit Mark of the Storm / Thundering Shuriken / Electrical Surge / Lightning Rush text

audit.why: The packet flagged 'His Slicing Maelstrom' in whys[4] as a probable wrong name at edit distance 4. It is a false positive — the flagged token is the possessive 'His', and Slicing Maelstrom is the real R name in the kit.
audit.corrected: No name change made; I dropped the possessive only because I was already rewriting the line for the cooldown.

edits.before: His Slicing Maelstrom is an AoE chain-stun and your CC lives in Mega, so this stage is whether Mega is up — bait his ult or E dash first.
edits.after: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s AoE chain-stun and your CC lives in Mega, so this stage is simply whether Mega is loaded — bait the ult first.

edits.before: Kennen sits at range and chips you with Q shurikens and Mark-stacking autos, so don't stand still and feed his poke — fight back. At level 1 trade autos when he steps up to last-hit, since one Q is his only ranged threat. Level 2 with Hyper is your window: land a Boomerang, get the third-consecutive-hit Hyper proc, and you out-chunk him before he can land three Marks for a stun. Through level 3 keep kiting with Q's slow and Hyper's move speed, and the first time Mega comes up, walk him down with a Wallop stun — his only escape is the Lightning Rush dash, and once it's down he can't peel off your slow.

Through level 3 kite with Q's slow and Hyper's move speed, and the first time Mega comes up, walk him down with a Wallop stun.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 hinge on Rage timing. If your bar lines up so Mega is available, you win hard — Wallop stuns him out of his kite or you wall-combo him with GNAR! for a kill while his E dash is down. The danger is getting caught in Mini with Rage on cooldown when Slicing Maelstrom lands; the ult's repeated stun pins fragile Mini Gnar in place and a full Kennen combo bursts you. So bait his ult or his Lightning Rush before you commit, and never take a level-6 trade unless Mega is loaded.

It is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so a spent ult hands you two clear minutes — never take a level-6 trade unless Mega is loaded.

edits.before: Once you hit your first item you out-tank his poke and run him down every Rage cycle Mega is up — close the lane here and snowball your kiting lead. Don't let it drag: a fed full-AP Kennen flanks with Lightning Rush, drops Slicing Maelstrom to chain-stun, and bursts your Mini form before you can transform. Your GNAR! wall-combo is the bigger teamfight swing one-for-one, but his AoE stun catches up front-to-back if you give him the items, so win early and group with your team.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape. All-in when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: matchup-defining — a flat 120s at every rank. Spent, and you own two minutes. - Lightning Rush is only 6-10s: an escape, not a window to plan around. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.
